content.text: Stripe's availability map covers 46 countries. PayPal's risk engine flags accounts from Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and dozens of other markets before any human review occurs. Gumroad holds payouts for up to 30 days in certain regions. Lemon Squeezy and Paddle are unavailable across most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. These are not temporary oversights waiting to be corrected — they are deliberate structural decisions built into conventional payment [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/full-infrastructure-guide-payment-infrastructure-south-asian-creators|COREMERCH guide to infrastructure]] designed for Western banking systems. The solution is not finding a workaround inside this system. It is building on infrastructure that does not have the problem in the first place. That means GitHub Pages or [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-webhook-driven-crypto-payment-fulfillment-explained-digital-4|Cloudflare Webhook-Driven]] Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/google-apps-script-digital-commerce-automation-explained-digital-5|google]] Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain payment verification. No platform can restrict access to a store that runs under your own accounts with no dependency on any payment processor.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Platform stripe

This isn't just a restriction; it's a fundamental issue of sovereignty, where platforms like Stripe and PayPal dictate what countries can and cannot use their services, essentially deciding who gets to sell and earn a living online. The term 'sovereign commerce infrastructure' refers to a self-owned, platform-independent solution that enables creators to deploy their own digital commerce stacks, free from the constraints of traditional payment processors. This means having full control over the entire infrastructure, from hosting to payment processing, and owning all the data. The goal is to provide a permanent structural alternative to the base layer, ensuring creators can continue to sell and grow their businesses without relying on platforms that can change their rules or ban their accounts at any time.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

At the heart of sovereign commerce infrastructure lies a combination of free and paid tools that work together seamlessly. GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages host the store, while Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script handle the backend logic, integrating with Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage and Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery. The payment processing is handled by NOWPayments, which supports 300+ cryptocurrencies and charges a 0.5% fee, making it an attractive option for creators in restricted countries. The infrastructure is designed to be fully customizable, allowing creators to scale their businesses as needed and stay in control of their data and finances.
Who This Is Built For and Why

This solution is specifically designed for digital creators in countries where Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle are unavailable or severely restricted. These creators sell ebooks, courses, templates, fonts, presets, beats, plugins, software, and digital products but cannot collect payment through conventional platforms. COREMERCH identifies with this struggle and aims to provide a permanent structural alternative that gives creators the freedom to operate and grow their businesses without relying on platforms that can change their rules or ban their accounts at any time.
Sovereign commerce infrastructure is not a workaround, but a permanent structural alternative to traditional payment processors.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The Edge Commerce Stack ($197) is a pre-configured solution that includes Cloudflare Pages, Workers, Supabase, and NOWPayments. This stack is deployed in 48 hours, includes 5 products loaded, SPF/DKIM/DMARC configured, and end-to-end testing before handoff. The Sovereign Starter Stack ($97) is another option, which includes GitHub Pages, Apps Script, and NOWPayments, deployed in 48 hours, with 3 products loaded and 30-day support. The Sovereign Blueprint ($47) offers complete documentation for all 5 stacks, including full source code and NOWPayments integration guide, while the Complete Builder Kit ($197) includes all 6 blueprints and 7 templates for instant download.
